neighbours.label: the word ' constellation' (and star-group names) in astronomy text
fire: On clear nights you can spot the constellation Cassiopeia overhead.
The new planet lies about 300 light-years away in the constellation Cygnus.
Ancient sailors navigated by the constellation known as the Plough.
Look east to find the bright constellation Taurus rising after dusk.
The meteor shower seems to come from the constellation Perseus.
Astronomers found a dwarf galaxy in the constellation Leo.
Every child in the class drew the constellation Orion on paper.
The comet will pass through the constellation Gemini next week.
quiet: On clear nights you can spot the planet Jupiter overhead.
The new planet lies about 300 light-years away from our Sun.
Ancient sailors navigated by the star known as Polaris.
Look east to find the bright full Moon rising after dusk.
The meteor shower seems to come from a single point in the sky.
Astronomers found a dwarf galaxy near the Milky Way.
Every child in the class drew the solar system on paper.
The comet will pass close to the Sun next week.

notes: ' constellation' 6 of top 32 plus Sigma/Alpha star designations; - pole is ' inter'(stellar).
